content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_no] [product_name] and would like to monitor the screen text on my PC using VB6 or Excel. Could someone please provide an example or explain how to do this? Thank you for your support.

It seems I haven't received assistance yet, so let me rephrase my question: How can I read the I/O values or status ([product_name] inputs/outputs) using a USB connector? I came across a data logging macro built with Excel for use with a serial connector (RS232), but it's not working on my PC. I need a quick solution.
Hello [user_name], Some posts in this thread reference data logging applications such as [product_name] Data Logger and [product_name] Monitor.

Thank you for your response. However, if you check the file I attached previously, you’ll see that I've already tried the suggested links but they did not work for me. I want to understand why that is the case, and also, is it possible to write new values to [product_name] using this macro?

Hi, Firstly, if the [product_name] Logger isn't working, I recommend reaching out to its developer for support—unfortunately, I don't have direct experience with it. From my understanding, the [product_name] Logger is designed solely to record the status of I/O and certain other signals to your PC in an Excel spreadsheet; it does not provide control functionality. Direct control is only available on specific [product_name] models together with an OPC Server. Hope this clarifies your query.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are looking for ways to monitor and interact with the screen display and I/O status of [product_name] modules from a PC, utilizing software like VB6 or Excel. Available options such as [product_name] Logger allow for data logging but do not support writing or controlling functions, and users have encountered compatibility and connectivity issues with USB versus RS232. The lack of integrated, simple solutions for both reading and writing I/O from a PC is negatively impacting users who desire immediate, bidirectional interaction.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to efficiently monitor and control I/O values of [product_name] devices from a PC using widely accessible interfaces (USB or serial) and familiar programs such as Excel or VB6.
